title: Pairwise Preference Evaluation + Slice Analysis for Reranking
content:
Purpose:
This doc describes the pairwise preference evaluation sets used for reranking model onboarding, explains how we compute NDCG from pairwise labels, and outlines the slice analysis and regression thresholds we run as part of model acceptance. Intended for applied-ml reviewers and solutions engineers running onboarding evaluations.

Summary of artifacts:
- Pairwise label CSVs: format = query_id, candidate_a_id, candidate_b_id, preferred (A|B|Tie or 1|0|0.5). Each file contains ~5k-50k judgments depending on model scope.
- Query metadata TSV: query_id, source, intent_tag, query_length_chars, domain (docs, faq, product, support), difficulty_bin (easy/med/hard).
- Gold relevance clusters (optional): for some datasets we provide cluster-level relevance labels to allow ordinal evaluation in addition to pairwise.

Labeling protocol (brief):
- Judgers shown query + two candidate outputs (A/B) in random order. Asked: "Which response would you prefer for this query?"
- Preference choices: A, B, Tie. Also collect a short freeform rationale and confidence (1-5).
- Each pair is judged by 3 raters. We keep raw labels for inter-annotator analysis and compute majority preference for scoring.
- Quality checks: gold control pairs inserted (~5% of pairs). Labelers failing controls >80% are excluded and cases re-annotated.

Converting pairwise prefs to ordinal scores (approach used in onboarding):
We support two pipelines depending on downstream needs:
1) Bradley-Terry (BT) model fit per query: Fit BT on the pairwise comparisons restricted to the query's candidate set to derive a latent score per candidate, then rank and compute NDCG from those scores. Good when we have many pairwise edges per query.
2) Borda-like aggregation: For smaller annotation budgets, convert majority pairwise outcomes into pairwise wins counts (wins - losses) and normalize to [0,1] to get pseudo-relevance scores. Simpler and faster when we have sparse pairs.
Notes: BT tends to be more stable when pairwise graph is dense; Borda is robust when there are ties and few edges. Both are implemented in the onboarding harness (see github PR linked above).

NDCG calculations used in release gating:
- Gain mapping: We map ordinal scores to relevance gains with a small nonlinear transform to emphasize top ranks: gain = floor(4 * score_normalized) where score_normalized in [0,1]. This maps to gains 0..4.
- Reported metrics: NDCG@1, NDCG@3, NDCG@5, and mean reciprocal rank (MRR) complementary.
- Bootstrapped confidence intervals: 1000 bootstrap resamples across queries; report 95% CI. Use query-level resampling (standard).

Slice definitions (for targeted regression detection):
- Intent slices: informational | transactional | navigational | support.
- Query length: short (<=20 chars), mid (21-80), long (>80).
- Domain: docs | faq | product | support | social.
- Difficulty: easy | med | hard (based on prior click entropy or annotator difficulty flag).
- Confidence bins: low (<3), med (3), high (4-5) — uses annotator confidence aggregated per pair.
- Edge-case behaviors: queries containing code fragments, math, or PII markers flagged as special slices.

Slice-level analysis to run for each model comparison:
- Per-slice NDCG@k delta vs baseline model with 95% bootstrapped CI. Flag slice if delta <= -0.015 (absolute) for any of NDCG@1/3/5.
- Per-slice win-rate of the candidate model in pairwise majority (>50% of majority-labeled pairs). Flag if win-rate < 45%.
- Inter-annotator agreement per slice (Kripp alpha or Cohen's kappa); warn if kappa < 0.35 — may indicate noisy labels.
- Example-driven debugging: for flagged slices, collect top 20 failing queries (largest absolute loss in DCG contribution) and surface to solutions-eng + PM.

Regression thresholds and gating rules (onboarding):
- Overall: model must have non-negative delta in NDCG@3 vs production baseline and not degrade lower bound of 95% CI by more than 0.01.
- Safety slices (PII/code/math): no degradation allowed, delta must be >= 0.
- Latency/cost tradeoff: If model improves NDCG by <0.01 but reduces cost/token by >15%, notify product for possible acceptance despite small quality delta.
- Human review: any flagged slice triggers required manual review and a short RCA before acceptance.

Example pairwise CSV row (literal example):
query_id,cand_a,cand_b,preferred,annotator_id,confidence,reason
q_20250301_017,doc_993,doc_412,A,ann_22,4,"A is more concise and directly answers the question"

Common pitfalls and caveats:
- Sparse pairwise graphs: When candidate sets per query are small (2-3 candidates) BT fitting can be unstable. Use Borda fallback and increase annotator redundancy.
- Ties handling: Ties are mapped to half-win for both candidates in win-count aggregation; in BT ties are recorded as 0.5/0.5 outcomes.
- Aggregation across queries: always do query-level normalization before averaging metrics; otherwise long candidate lists can dominate.

Practical checklist to run an onboarding eval (quick):
1) Gather candidate sets for sample queries (Nqueries target = 2k-10k depending on product).
2) Generate randomized A/B pair permutations and inject gold controls.
3) Run annotation job (3x redundancy).
4) Run data quality pass (kappa, control filter).
5) Convert pairwise -> scores (BT or Borda).
6) Compute NDCG@1/3/5 + bootstrap CI and slice deltas vs baseline.
7) If any slice flagged, run manual review and prepare RCAs.
8) Produce onboarding report (template link in Confluence).

Open questions / TODOs:
- Decide standard gain mapping for new product verticals (current floor(4*score) may not be optimal). TODO: experiment with continuous gains (2^rel -1) for next cycle (owner: Ben Cho).
- Evaluate automated triage rules that escalate slices with small absolute delta but many failing queries. (owner: Marina)
- Add scripted visualization bundle (per-slice waterfall charts + per-query DCG contributions) to the CI harness.

References and links:
- Onboarding harness (local): github.com/redwood-inference/rerank-eval
- Confluence playbook: linked above.
- JIRA epic: JIRA-RANK-412 (onboarding + regression infra)

Notes to reviewers:
- This doc intentionally favors practical heuristics over formal research-level claims; please call out if you want more statistical rigor for the gating rules.
- If you want to reproduce the experiments in the next PR, run the script eval/run_pairwise_to_ndcg.py with --bootstrap 1000 --bt-fit-threshold 6.

-- Aisha
